messages:
elaine: Customer on private VPC can't complete onprem installer. Installer logs show failures pulling model shards and telemetry. Error snippets mention TLS handshake failures and 403 from S3 presigned URLs. They have a strict egress allowlist. Can we provide a minimal hostlist + ports + OCSP/SNI endpoints? attaching curl repro.

samir: thx — can you paste the exact error block and installer version?

elaine: installer v0.63.2. root log:
```
2026-03-15T12:23:01Z error: fetch shard https://models-us-east-1.s3.amazonaws.com/redwood/gpt-4r/part-000 failed: TLS handshake: certificate verify failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2026-03-15T12:23:02Z warn: telemetry upload failed: POST https://telemetry.redwood.ai/v1/events 408
```

maria: If they're doing TLS-inspection/proxy MITM that's the most likely cause for x509 errors. For allowlist we recommend FQDNs (443) plus DNS/OCSP/NTP. Minimal hostlist we usually provide: 
- models: *.s3.amazonaws.com, models-*.s3.amazonaws.com (443)
- registry/metadata: registry.redwood.ai (443)
- auth: auth.redwood.ai, token.redwood.ai (443)
- telemetry: telemetry.redwood.ai (443)
- packages: pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org (443), artifactory.redwood.ai or customer Artifactory host (443)
- apt: deb.debian.org, security.debian.org (443)
- OCSP/CRL endpoints referenced by cert chains (eg. ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org)
Also allow DNS (53 UDP/TCP) and NTP (123 UDP) for reliable ops.

oncall: important note: if they cannot disable TLS intercept they need to import the proxy CA into the instance trust store (or have the proxy passthrough for those hosts). Otherwise curl/openssl will always fail.

elaine: customer asked for IP ranges instead of hostnames — do we publish fixed IPs for registry/telemetry/s3?

samir: we don't guarantee fixed public IPs for S3; recommend FQDN allowlist. If they insist on IPs: use AWS IP ranges for the region (eg. us-east-1 prefixes) + our telemetry/public endpoints CIDR (we can provide telemetry CIDR on enterprise contract). Also note presigned S3 URLs will point to s3 endpoints or cloudfront.

maria: reproduction curl they can run inside the VPC to verify egress/TLS path:
```
curl -vS --resolve registry.redwood.ai:443:18.205.93.1 https://registry.redwood.ai/health
```
Look for a TLS handshake and an HTTP/200. If they see "unable to get local issuer certificate" or "certificate has unknown authority" that's TLS interception.

elaine: I sent the hostlist + suggested curl checks. Customer ran curl and returned: "SSL: certificate: unable to get local issuer certificate" — confirmed TLS MITM. They're asking whether we can skip TLS validation in the installer.

samir: we do NOT recommend or ship installers that skip certificate verification. That's a security risk. Options: 1) import MITM CA into OS trust store (preferred), 2) configure proxy passthrough for Redwood hosts, 3) use our offline enterprise installer tarball (requires ticket/contract).

infra-bot: ticket created: KB-2309 "Onprem installer egress checklist" — https://kb.redwood.ai/kb/2309 (internal).

oncall: if customer can't change proxy settings, escalate to account exec for offline/airgapped option. I can prepare an ephemeral offline bundle if procurement approves.

maria: adding OCSP and Artifactory CIDRs to the note. Also remind them to allow TCP/443 with SNI preserved; some proxies rewrite SNI and break HTTP virtual hosts.

elaine: customer acknowledged and will test after importing the proxy CA. Will update thread tomorrow. :thumbsup:
